video.description:
MCP is an open protocol that standardizes how applications provide context to LLMs. Think of MCP like a USB-C port for AI applications. Just as USB-C provides a standardized way to connect your devices to various peripherals and accessories, MCP provides a standardized way to connect AI models to different data sources and tools.

video.title: 10. Agentic Engineering - Model Context Protocol (MCP)
video.rationale: Covers: topic ✓ (0:00–1:30), CO1.LO2 ✓ (0:00–1:30) [from transcript] · Agentic Engineering Course · tier 4 · 16:05 · 21 views · captions
video.description:
These slides are based on Chapter 10 of the book Agentic Engineering from First Principles, available at https://agentic-engineering-book.com/#book-download

Watch the full course in order: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLcgj6DgXMS5A

The question: How can an agent discover and invoke external capabilities through a standard interface, instead of a custom integration for every system?

By the end of this lecture, you will have traced every message involved in one MCP tool call. And you'll know which questions the protocol answers, and which it leaves to the host.

Chapter principle: MCP standardizes capability access. It does not create agency.

Model Context Protocol (MCP) is the open standard *"universal adapter"* that empowers AI agents to overcome static training data by securely and uniformly connecting with the real world's live data and actionable tools. video.title: How Model Context Protocol (MCP) actually works
video.rationale: Covers: topic ✓ (0:04–1:34), CO1.LO2 ✗ [from transcript] · Google Cloud Tech · tier 2 · 7:58 · 400,997 views · captions
video.description:
Google MCPs → https://goo.gle/3PYkjky 
Build an ADK agent with Google MCPs → https://goo.gle/4o6h8DP 
Connect an MCP server to an AI agent → https://goo.gle/4uk7YW2 

APIs were built for deterministic programs, but AI models reason probabilistically. So how do you get your AI agents to talk to your tools and data without writing messy, custom integration code every time? Enter the Model Context Protocol (MCP). In this video, Smitha Kolan explains what MCP is, how it standardizes the way AI models discover and interact with external resources, and why it's becoming the new standard over traditional APIs for AI-powered applications
